verses: ٱقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِى غَفْلَةٍ مُّعْرِضُونَ
مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِم مُّحْدَثٍ إِلَّا ٱسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ
لَاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ هَلْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ أَفَتَأْتُونَ ٱلسِّحْرَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ
قَالَ رَبِّى يَعْلَمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
بَلْ قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَٰثُ أَحْلَٰمٍۭ بَلِ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِـَٔايَةٍ كَمَآ أُرْسِلَ ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ
مَآ ءَامَنَتْ قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَآ أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ
وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ فَسْـَٔلُوٓا۟ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
وَمَا جَعَلْنَٰهُمْ جَسَدًا لَّا يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰلِدِينَ
ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْوَعْدَ فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُمْ وَمَن نَّشَآءُ وَأَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
لَقَدْ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَٰبًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً وَأَنشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا ءَاخَرِينَ
فَلَمَّآ أَحَسُّوا۟ بَأْسَنَآ إِذَا هُم مِّنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ
لَا تَرْكُضُوا۟ وَٱرْجِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَآ أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ وَمَسَٰكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْـَٔلُونَ
قَالُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
فَمَا زَالَت تِّلْكَ دَعْوَىٰهُمْ حَتَّىٰ جَعَلْنَٰهُمْ حَصِيدًا خَٰمِدِينَ
وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَٰعِبِينَ
لَوْ أَرَدْنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لَّٱتَّخَذْنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّآ إِن كُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِٱلْحَقِّ عَلَى ٱلْبَٰطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُۥ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ وَلَكُمُ ٱلْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ
وَلَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَنْ عِندَهُۥ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِۦ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ
يُسَبِّحُونَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ
أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَةً مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنشِرُونَ
لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ ءَالِهَةٌ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا فَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
لَا يُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْـَٔلُونَ
أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَٰنَكُمْ هَٰذَا ذِكْرُ مَن مَّعِىَ وَذِكْرُ مَن قَبْلِى بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْحَقَّ فَهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ
وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدُونِ
وَقَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ بَلْ عِبَادٌ مُّكْرَمُونَ
لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُۥ بِٱلْقَوْلِ وَهُم بِأَمْرِهِۦ يَعْمَلُونَ
يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ٱرْتَضَىٰ وَهُم مِّنْ خَشْيَتِهِۦ مُشْفِقُونَ
وَمَن يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّىٓ إِلَٰهٌ مِّن دُونِهِۦ فَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
وَجَعَلْنَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ
وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ سَقْفًا مَّحْفُوظًا وَهُمْ عَنْ ءَايَٰتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِى فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ
وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ ٱلْخُلْدَ أَفَإِي۟ن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلْخَٰلِدُونَ
كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ وَنَبْلُوكُم بِٱلشَّرِّ وَٱلْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ
وَإِذَا رَءَاكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى يَذْكُرُ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَهُم بِذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ هُمْ كَٰفِرُونَ
خُلِقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ سَأُو۟رِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِى فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
لَوْ يَعْلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَن وُجُوهِهِمُ ٱلنَّارَ وَلَا عَن ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
بَلْ تَأْتِيهِم بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنظَرُونَ
وَلَقَدِ ٱسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِٱلَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا۟ مِنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
قُلْ مَن يَكْلَؤُكُم بِٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ بَلْ هُمْ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِم مُّعْرِضُونَ
أَمْ لَهُمْ ءَالِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُم مِّن دُونِنَا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَا هُم مِّنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ
بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَءَابَآءَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْعُمُرُ أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِى ٱلْأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَآ أَفَهُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أُنذِرُكُم بِٱلْوَحْىِ وَلَا يَسْمَعُ ٱلصُّمُّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا مَا يُنذَرُونَ
وَلَئِن مَّسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْـًٔا وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ
وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَآءً وَذِكْرًا لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَهُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ
وَهَٰذَا ذِكْرٌ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ أَفَأَنتُمْ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ
وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ رُشْدَهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَٰلِمِينَ
إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنتُمْ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ
قَالُوا۟ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا لَهَا عَٰبِدِينَ
قَالَ لَقَدْ كُنتُمْ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُمْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
قَالُوٓا۟ أَجِئْتَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّٰعِبِينَ
قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمْ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۠ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَّهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ
قَالُوا۟ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُۥٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ
قَالُوا۟ فَأْتُوا۟ بِهِۦ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ
قَالُوٓا۟ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلْتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَٰذَا فَسْـَٔلُوهُمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ يَنطِقُونَ
فَرَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّكُمْ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ
قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
أُفٍّ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
قَالُوا۟ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ
قُلْنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِى بَرْدًا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
وَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ
وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَلُوطًا إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَٰلَمِينَ
وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا صَٰلِحِينَ
وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَإِقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا عَٰبِدِينَ
وَلُوطًا ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِى كَانَت تَّعْمَلُ ٱلْخَبَٰٓئِثَ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَٰسِقِينَ
وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
وَنُوحًا إِذْ نَادَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
وَنَصَرْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
وَدَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِى ٱلْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلْقَوْمِ وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَٰهِدِينَ
فَفَهَّمْنَٰهَا سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَكُلًّا ءَاتَيْنَا حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُۥدَ ٱلْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَٱلطَّيْرَ وَكُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
وَعَلَّمْنَٰهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَّكُمْ لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ فَهَلْ أَنتُمْ شَٰكِرُونَ
وَلِسُلَيْمَٰنَ ٱلرِّيحَ عَاصِفَةً تَجْرِى بِأَمْرِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا وَكُنَّا بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَٰلِمِينَ
وَمِنَ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ مَن يَغُوصُونَ لَهُۥ وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَٰفِظِينَ
وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِۦ مِن ضُرٍّ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَٰبِدِينَ
وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُۨجِى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
وَزَكَرِيَّآ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِى فَرْدًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُۥ زَوْجَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا خَٰشِعِينَ
وَٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهَا مِن رُّوحِنَا وَجَعَلْنَٰهَا وَٱبْنَهَآ ءَايَةً لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَٰحِدَةً وَأَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُونِ
وَتَقَطَّعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ كُلٌّ إِلَيْنَا رَٰجِعُونَ
فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِۦ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ كَٰتِبُونَ
وَحَرَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَآ أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ وَهُم مِّن كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنسِلُونَ
وَٱقْتَرَبَ ٱلْوَعْدُ ٱلْحَقُّ فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ هَٰذَا بَلْ كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ أَنتُمْ لَهَا وَٰرِدُونَ
لَوْ كَانَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ءَالِهَةً مَّا وَرَدُوهَا وَكُلٌّ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وَهُمْ فِيهَا لَا يَسْمَعُونَ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُم مِّنَّا ٱلْحُسْنَىٰٓ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ
لَا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَهَا وَهُمْ فِى مَا ٱشْتَهَتْ أَنفُسُهُمْ خَٰلِدُونَ
لَا يَحْزُنُهُمُ ٱلْفَزَعُ ٱلْأَكْبَرُ وَتَتَلَقَّىٰهُمُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ هَٰذَا يَوْمُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى كُنتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ
يَوْمَ نَطْوِى ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَطَىِّ ٱلسِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ كَمَا بَدَأْنَآ أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُّعِيدُهُۥ وَعْدًا عَلَيْنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنَا فِى ٱلزَّبُورِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ٱلذِّكْرِ أَنَّ ٱلْأَرْضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِىَ ٱلصَّٰلِحُونَ
إِنَّ فِى هَٰذَا لَبَلَٰغًا لِّقَوْمٍ عَٰبِدِينَ
وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ إِلَّا رَحْمَةً لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
قُلْ إِنَّمَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ فَهَلْ أَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ
فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟ فَقُلْ ءَاذَنتُكُمْ عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍ وَإِنْ أَدْرِىٓ أَقَرِيبٌ أَم بَعِيدٌ مَّا تُوعَدُونَ
إِنَّهُۥ يَعْلَمُ ٱلْجَهْرَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْتُمُونَ
وَإِنْ أَدْرِى لَعَلَّهُۥ فِتْنَةٌ لَّكُمْ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قَٰلَ رَبِّ ٱحْكُم بِٱلْحَقِّ وَرَبُّنَا ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ

leads.title: Abraham smashes the idols
leads.summary: In Genesis Rabbah, Abraham smashes the idols in his father's shop, blames the largest one, and is thrown into a furnace by Nimrod. In the Quran, Abraham breaks the idols except the biggest, tells the people to ask them, and is thrown into a fire made cool.

leads.title: Utnapishtim's flood (Gilgamesh, Standard Babylonian Tablet XI:8-206) ↔ Noah answered; David and Solomon's judgment, the praising mountains, mail and wind
leads.summary: 2 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: All others perish (weight 5.9); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). Pair score 11.3.

Only in Utnapishtim's flood (Gilgamesh, Standard Babylonian Tablet XI:8-206): The divine warning commands: abandon riches, spurn property and save life; After the flood all humankind has returned to clay; the plain is flat as a roof; Instead of the flood, a lion, a wolf, famine or plague should have diminished the people; The mother goddess bars the god who caused the flood from the offering, for he acted without counsel; Huge measured quantities of bitumen, pitch and oil are poured into the kiln and the hull; The hero slaughters oxen and sheep and gives the workers beer, oil and wine like river water, so they feast as at the New Year festival; What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer; The chief god sees the boat and is enraged that a living being escaped: 'no man should survive!'; What the ark contains; Besides kin and animals, craftsmen of every skill are taken aboard; The god gives the hero a cover story: Enlil hates me, I am going down to the Apsû, and he will rain abundance on you (bread-cakes in the morning, a torrent of wheat in the evening) - an ambiguous promise of the coming flood; How the ark is described; and 79 more.

Only in Noah answered; David and Solomon's judgment, the praising mountains, mail and wind: David and Solomon judge a case of sheep that strayed by night into a field; Solomon is given the right understanding; God taught David the craft of making coats of mail [contrast between the texts]; The people see that divine wisdom is in the king to do justice; The people see that divine wisdom is in the king to do justice [divergence between the texts]; Liability for one's grazing animals or spreading fire damaging another's field; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David [divergence between the texts]; A herdsman's sheep graze in a cultivator's field [divergence between the texts]; God taught David the craft of making coats of mail; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents [divergence between the texts]; The stormy wind is subjected to Solomon, blowing at his command; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David; Devils (shayāṭīn) and jinn labor for Solomon, diving and building; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/ane-quran/22-ane-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A balance set upright / just balances set up for the judgment (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in BD 125 (pNu): address to the gods of the hall, works of mercy, purity and the examination at the gate: Giving food to the hungry (water, clothing, a ferry) as the deed that justifies before the judge; Self-praise: I did what people speak of and what the gods are pleased with; I satisfied the god with what he loves; Self-praise of the just: I gave bread to the hungry, water to the thirsty, clothes to the naked (and a ferry to the boatless); A fixed day on which the characters or deeds of the dead are reckoned up before the god of the dead; The judge's messengers inflict slaughter and punishment, and there is no mercy in their faces; The dead has purified himself in a sacred lake (the southern pool, the field of locusts) where the gods' crew washes; Catalogue of the righteous man: no eating on the mountains, no idols, no adultery, no menstrual intercourse, no oppression, returns pledges, feeds the hungry, clothes the naked, no interest; The just one's front, back and middle are pure; no limb of his is without Maat; Gate-guardians interrogate the dead: who are you, what is your name, where did you pass, what did you see, what did they give you?; The just one lives on Maat and feeds on Maat; the divine judges too are said to live on Maat, with no lie in their bodies; Who witnesses against the dead at the judgment (no witness against me / their own limbs and skins) [divergence between the texts]; In the judgment of the dead the heart is weighed on a balance against Maat; Anubis checks the plummet and Thoth records the result; and 6 more.

Only in The split heavens, water of life, orbits, mortality and the scales: Man was created of haste; God comes to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; Whether a human, such as the flood hero, is granted eternal life; God gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion (al-furqān), a light and reminder; When the gods created mankind they allotted death to them and kept life in their own hands; At the beginning heaven and earth, once together, were separated; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq); The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; God made the sky a protected roof; 'Let God weigh me in just balances and know my integrity' [divergence between the texts]; God made every living thing from water; and 12 more.

matches.note: Upelluri: 'when heaven and earth were built on me ... when they cut heaven and earth apart with the cutting tool (URUDU kuruzzit arḫa kuerer)'; Ea has 'the ancient saw with which they cut heaven and earth apart (nepiš tekann-a kuēz arḫa kuerer)' brought out. 21:30: 'the heavens and the earth were one closed mass (ratqan) and We split them apart (fa-fataqnāhumā)'. Same act on the same pair; the Hittite gives a tool and an unnamed 'they', the Quran no tool and a first-person God.

leads.title: Woe to Ariel; enemies like a dream; the sealed book; lip service; the potter and the clay ↔ The reckoning approaches; mortal messengers and destroyed towns
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The people's reckoning draws near while they turn away in heedlessness (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Woe to Ariel; enemies like a dream; the sealed book; lip service; the potter and the clay: Jerusalem called 'Ariel' (altar-hearth / lion of God), the city where David camped, to be besieged and become 'like an ariel'; The multitude of nations fighting Zion will be like a dream of the night: like a hungry man who dreams he eats and wakes empty; YHWH 'who redeemed Abraham' (a deliverance of Abraham alluded to); Vision is like a sealed book: the literate cannot read it because it is sealed, the illiterate because he cannot read; God pours out a spirit of deep sleep (tardemah) and shuts the eyes of prophets and seers; The humbled city's voice will come from the ground like a ghost's (ov) and chirp from the dust; God will do wonders so that the wisdom of the wise perishes and the understanding of the prudent is hidden; They hide from people but not from God, who is with them when they plot by night; In a little while Lebanon will become a fruitful field (Carmel) and the field be counted a forest; Shall the clay say to the potter 'he did not make me' or 'he has no understanding'?; Revelation as a sealed or an open book [contrast between the texts]; God seals the sleepers' ears (puts them to sleep) in the cave for many years; and 11 more.

Only in The reckoning approaches; mortal messengers and destroyed towns: The doomed townsfolk run from God's onslaught and are told mockingly to return to their luxuries; they become mown stubble; The punished cry 'woe (ahula / yā waylanā), we have sinned (been wrongdoers)'; 'Ask the people of the Reminder (ahl al-dhikr) if you do not know': appeal to earlier scripture-holders; Earlier messengers were only men who ate food and were not immortal; Opponents call the revelation jumbled dreams, a forgery, or the work of a poet; The unbelievers demand: 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?'; The slain are piled up in heaps like grain stacks or sheaves; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: All the host of heaven rot away and the heavens roll up like a scroll; their host falls like withered leaves from vine and fig (weight 7.1). Pair score 7.1.

Only in Judgment on the nations and Edom; heavens rolled up like a scroll; Lilith in the ruins: 'Seek in the book of YHWH and read: not one of these is missing'; God has allotted the land to the wild creatures by lot; A day of vengeance for YHWH, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion; God's sword has drunk its fill in heaven and descends on Edom, sated with blood and fat as at a sacrifice in Bozrah; Edom's streams turned to pitch and soil to brimstone; its smoke goes up forever, night and day unquenched; In the ruins goat-demons call to each other and Lilith (lilit) settles and finds herself a resting place; God stretches over the land the measuring line of chaos (tohu) and the plummet of emptiness (bohu); The damned wear garments of pitch (qatiran), fire covering their faces; All the host of heaven rot away and the heavens roll up like a scroll; their host falls like withered leaves from vine and fig [divergence between the texts]; God himself devotes the nations (or a nation) to destruction (herem) and gives them to slaughter; Land made brimstone and salt like Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim; On the day the sky heaves (tamur) and the mountains move away; God's flashing sword devours flesh and his arrows are drunk with blood; and 2 more.

Only in One community, Gog and Magog, the rolled heaven and the Zabur's promise: On the day of the great terror the angels meet the righteous: 'This is your day that you were promised'; The idolaters and what they worship are fuel (ḥaṣab) for hell; The prophet was sent only as a mercy to the worlds; As God began the first creation he will repeat it; Gog and Magog are let loose and swarm down from every height before the end; Humanity was one community (umma) but split its affair into sects; A savage people is let loose and pours down from the mountains or heights [divergence between the texts]; The heavens are folded like cloth or a scroll before or by the deity; Gog and Magog are let loose and swarm down from every height before the end [divergence between the texts]; Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince (nesi rosh) of Meshech and Tubal, an eschatological invader; The meek / those who wait for YHWH / the righteous and their seed shall inherit the land (yirshu arets).

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; God looks at the earth and it trembles, touches the mountains and they smoke; and 39 more.

Only in The split heavens, water of life, orbits, mortality and the scales: Man was created of haste; A balance set upright / just balances set up for the judgment; God comes to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; Whether a human, such as the flood hero, is granted eternal life; God gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion (al-furqān), a light and reminder; When the gods created mankind they allotted death to them and kept life in their own hands; At the beginning heaven and earth, once together, were separated; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq); The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; God made the sky a protected roof; 'Let God weigh me in just balances and know my integrity' [divergence between the texts]; and 11 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God taught David the craft of making coats of mail (weight 6.7); Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David (weight 6.3); The stormy wind is subjected to Solomon, blowing at his command (weight 6.3); Devils (shayāṭīn) and jinn labor for Solomon, diving and building (weight 6.0). Pair score 25.3.

Only in Noah answered; David and Solomon's judgment, the praising mountains, mail and wind: The people see that divine wisdom is in the king to do justice; Hero's family saved with him; Liability for one's grazing animals or spreading fire damaging another's field; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; David and Solomon judge a case of sheep that strayed by night into a field; Solomon is given the right understanding; All others perish.

Only in David's mountains and mail; Solomon's wind, copper, jinn and staff: A great cast-bronze 'sea' basin rests on twelve bronze oxen facing the four directions in threes; God made a spring of molten copper (or brass) flow for Solomon; The jinn did not know the unseen, else they would not have stayed in humiliating labor; Rivers clap their hands and mountains sing together before YHWH; Solomon dies leaning on his staff; only a creature of the earth gnawing the staff reveals his death when he falls; Two golden cherubim face each other with wings spread over the ark.

leads.summary: 2 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The fire does not harm the hero (weight 6.8); Hero thrown into a fire or furnace by a king or people (weight 6.2). Pair score 13.1.

Only in Abraham and the idols in the Quran: Hero blames the largest idol for the destruction; Hero reasons from the stars, moon and sun to the one God; Hero smashes or burns idols; Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols.

Only in The golden image and the fiery furnace: God sends his angel to rescue his servants from death; All are commanded to bow to the king's image on pain of being thrown into a blazing furnace; The flames kill the men who throw the heroes into the furnace; A fourth figure appears walking in the fire, looking like a son of the gods (bar elahin); The furnace is heated seven times more than usual; The king sets up a golden image sixty cubits high and six wide on the plain of Dura; Envious courtiers 'eat the pieces' (slander) of the Jews and denounce their non-compliance to the king; The pagan king decrees that anyone who blasphemes or fails to fear the Jewish God will be punished; The rescued have not a hair singed, their garments unchanged, and no smell of fire on them; Long repeated list of imperial officials (satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates); A listed orchestra of instruments (horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, symphonia) signals the moment to bow to the idol; The faithful declare that God can save them, but even if he does not, they will not serve the king's gods; and 6 more.

וּ֠מִֽתְכַּנְּשִׁין אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֞א סִגְנַיָּ֣א וּפַחֲוָתָא֮ וְהַדָּבְרֵ֣י מַלְכָּא֒ חָזַ֣יִן לְגֻבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֡ךְ דִּי֩ לָֽא שְׁלֵ֨ט נוּרָ֜א בְּגֶשְׁמְה֗וֹן וּשְׂעַ֤ר רֵֽאשְׁהוֹן֙ לָ֣א הִתְחָרַ֔ךְ וְסָרְבָּלֵיה֖וֹן לָ֣א שְׁנ֑וֹ וְרֵ֣יחַ נ֔וּר לָ֥א עֲדָ֖ת בְּהֽוֹן

passages.text: (3:20) וּלְגֻבְרִ֤ין גִּבָּֽרֵי חַ֨יִל֙ דִּ֣י בְחַיְלֵ֔הּ אֲמַר֙ לְכַפָּתָ֔ה לְשַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ לְמִרְמֵ֕א לְאַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא (3:21) בֵּאדַ֜יִן גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ךְ כְּפִ֨תוּ֙ בְּסַרְבָּלֵיהוֹן֙ פטישיהון פַּטְּשֵׁיה֔וֹן וְכַרְבְּלָתְה֖וֹן וּלְבֻשֵׁיה֑וֹן וּרְמִ֕יו לְגֽוֹא אַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא (3:22) כָּל קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָ֗ה מִן דִּ֞י מִלַּ֤ת מַלְכָּא֙ מַחְצְפָ֔ה וְאַתּוּנָ֖א אֵזֵ֣ה יַתִּ֑ירָא גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ךְ דִּ֤י הַסִּ֨קוּ֙ לְשַׁדְרַ֤ךְ מֵישַׁךְ֙ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֔וֹ קַטִּ֣ל הִמּ֔וֹן שְׁבִיבָ֖א דִּ֥י נוּרָֽא (3:23) וְגֻבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ תְּלָ֣תֵּה֔וֹן שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ נְפַ֛לוּ לְגֽוֹא אַתּוּן נוּרָ֥א יָֽקִדְתָּ֖א מְכַפְּתִֽין

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֡שׁ לְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר עָמְד֨וּ עָלָ֜יו הַאַתֶּ֣ם תְּרִיב֣וּן לַבַּ֗עַל אִם אַתֶּם֙ תּוֹשִׁיע֣וּן אוֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥יב ל֛וֹ יוּמַ֖ת עַד הַבֹּ֑קֶר אִם אֱלֹהִ֥ים הוּא֙ יָ֣רֶב ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת מִזְבְּחֽוֹ
וַיִּקְרָא ל֥וֹ בַיּוֹם הַה֖וּא יְרֻבַּ֣עַל לֵאמֹ֑ר יָ֤רֶב בּוֹ֙ הַבַּ֔עַל כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת מִזְבְּחֽוֹ

sides.note: The same argument from the idol's helplessness: ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreb lô kî nātaṣ ʾet-mizbəḥô, 'if he is a god let him contend for himself'; bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fa-sʾalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūn, 'ask them, if they can speak'. In Judg the idolatrous father Joash says it to protect his son; in Q Abraham says it to shame the people, and they are turned on their heads (nukisū ʿalā ruʾūsihim).

passages.text: (6:25) וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֨עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת (6:26) וּבָנִ֨יתָ מִזְבֵּ֜חַ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ עַ֣ל רֹ֧אשׁ הַמָּע֛וֹז הַזֶּ֖ה בַּמַּֽעֲרָכָ֑ה וְלָֽקַחְתָּ֙ אֶת הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהַעֲלִ֣יתָ עוֹלָ֔ה בַּעֲצֵ֥י הָאֲשֵׁרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּכְרֹֽת (6:27) וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה (6:28) וַיַּשְׁכִּ֜ימוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֤ה נֻתַּץ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַבַּ֔עַל וְהָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו כֹּרָ֑תָה וְאֵת֙ הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֹֽעֲלָ֔ה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ הַבָּנֽוּי

וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֨עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת

וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה

leads.summary: أَصْنام (ʾaṣnām, “idol”) occurs in 5 verses, all or nearly all inside two narratives: Abraham (4) and Moses (1). A rare word linking two stories.

passages.text: وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ ءَازَرَ أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَامًا ءَالِهَةً إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰكَ وَقَوْمَكَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ

وَجَٰوَزْنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَتَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍ يَعْكُفُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَصْنَامٍ لَّهُمْ قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَى ٱجْعَل لَّنَآ إِلَٰهًا كَمَا لَهُمْ ءَالِهَةٌ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ
وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدَ ءَامِنًا وَٱجْنُبْنِى وَبَنِىَّ أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلْأَصْنَامَ
وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَٰكِفِينَ
